articles.title: Spotify says it’s working with labels on ‘responsible’ AI music tools
articles.summary: Sony, Universal, Warner and other music labels are partnering with Spotify as it starts a generative AI ‘research lab.’
articles.body: The recently-rumored AI partnership between Spotify and the major record labels is now a reality. The streaming service announced today that it’s entering into an agreement with Sony Music Group, Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group, Merlin, and Believe to develop “responsible AI products.” Unfortunately, your guess is as good as ours as to what exactly that means. Spotify didn’t detail any specific products in the works but said it was building a “state-of-the-art generative AI research lab and product team focused on developing technologies that reflect our principles and create breakthrough experiences for fans and artists.” Most of the press release is dedicated to vagaries and laying out the principles that will guide Spotify’s generative AI projects: * Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We’ll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later. * Choice in participation: We recognize there’s a wide range of views on use of generative music tools within the artistic community. Therefore, artists and rightsholders will choose if and how to participate to ensure the use of AI tools aligns with the values of the people behind the music. * Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for uses of their work and transparently credited for their contributions. * Artist-fan connection: AI tools we develop will not replace human artistry. They will give artists new ways to be creative and connect with fans. We will leverage our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections. Spotify has already come under fire for its handling of AI slop proliferating on its platform, and its in-house AI products, like a personalized DJ and NotebookLM-powered 2024 Spotify Wrapped podcast, have been relatively limited so far. Also, many artists would argue that the company’s definition of “fair compensation” is laughable. And for all the press releases’ talk about how “copyright is essential,” Spotify has been on the defensive end of accusations of copyright infringement on multiple occasions.

articles.title: Mick Jagger, 83 años, entrena de cinco a seis días a la semana y corre 12 kilómetros al día: "Me acuesto a las dos de la madrugada y me levanto a las diez de la mañana"
articles.standfirst: El líder de The Rolling Stones revela los hábitos de ejercicio, dieta y descanso que le mantienen en plena forma
articles.summary: El líder de The Rolling Stones revela los hábitos de ejercicio, dieta y descanso que le mantienen en plena forma
articles.body: Mick Jagger sigue desafiando al paso del tiempo. A sus 83 años, el líder de The Rolling Stones mantiene una rutina de entrenamiento propia de un deportista de élite: se ejercita entre cinco y seis días por semana y cuida al detalle su alimentación y su descanso. Esa disciplina es la que le permite seguir dándolo todo sobre el escenario, donde puede llegar a recorrer hasta 19 kilómetros en un solo concierto. Lejos quedan los excesos de sus primeros años en el rock. El cantante británico ha apostado por un estilo de vida enfocado en la longevidad y en el bienestar físico y mental, una transformación que explica buena parte de su sorprendente vitalidad. Jagger trabaja bajo la supervisión de un entrenador especializado en atletas de alto rendimiento. Su programa combina disciplinas muy distintas con un objetivo claro: ganar fondo, fuerza y flexibilidad. Alterna sesiones de musculación con carrera, sprints, ciclismo, natación e incluso kickboxing. A esa base se suman clases de danza y de ballet clásico, fundamentales para conservar la postura, el equilibrio y la agilidad que exhibe en cada actuación. Completa su rutina con yoga y pilates, dos prácticas que le ayudan a mejorar la movilidad de las articulaciones y a reducir el estrés. La alimentación es otro de los pilares de su forma física. Su dieta se basa en productos ecológicos y en hidratos de carbono complejos de calidad, como el arroz integral, el pan artesanal y las legumbres, que le aportan energía de forma sostenida. El músico dejó atrás las drogas y, a los 58 años, redujo de forma drástica el consumo de alcohol, consciente de que debía cuidar su cuerpo a largo plazo. El descanso tampoco se negocia. Jagger sigue un horario de sueño estricto: se acuesta en torno a las dos de la madrugada y se levanta a las diez, lo que le garantiza unas ocho horas de sueño para recuperar los músculos y llegar con la mente despejada a sus compromisos. Su caso demuestra que constancia, buena alimentación y descanso son claves para envejecer con salud.

articles.title: Cine Odeon reabre nesta quinta; reinauguração tem ingressos esgotados | G1
articles.standfirst: A reabertura faz parte da primeira fase do programa Reviver Cinema, da Prefeitura do Rio, com a Secretaria Municipal de Cultura e a RioFilme, voltado à revitalização dos cinemas de rua da cidade.
articles.summary: A reabertura faz parte da primeira fase do programa Reviver Cinema, da Prefeitura do Rio, com a Secretaria Municipal de Cultura e a RioFilme.
articles.body:
O Cine Odeon, na Cinelândia, Centro do Rio, um dos mais tradicionais da cidade, reabre nesta quinta-feira (29) após seis anos sem programação regular. A reabertura será com a exibição do filme “Feito Pipa”, candidato a representar o Brasil no Oscar 2027 . Os ingressos para as duas sessões desta quinta, entretanto, estão esgotados.

A reabertura faz parte da primeira fase do programa Reviver Cinema, da Prefeitura do Rio, com a Secretaria Municipal de Cultura e a RioFilme, voltado à revitalização dos cinemas de rua da cidade. O Odeon pertence ao grupo Severiano Ribeiro/Kinoplex e completa cem anos em 2026.

Quem perdeu a oportunidade, entretanto, terá outras chances. Até 4 de novembro, os ingressos para filmes do Odeon custam R$ 12. A partir do dia 5, o valor será de R$ 15 para qualquer público e sessão. A programação ainda será divulgada.

Inaugurado em 1926, o Cine Odeon, na Cinelândia, é um dos símbolos da época em que grandes salas de exibição transformaram o Centro do Rio em um polo cinematográfico. Construído no terreno do antigo Convento da Ajuda, o cinema integrava o chamado “quarteirão dos palácios de cinema”, cuja concentração de salas deu nome à região. Após períodos de fechamento e reformas, tornou-se uma das principais casas do Festival do Rio, desde a primeira edição do evento, em 1999. Em 2015, passou a se chamar Cine Odeon — Centro Cultural Luiz Severiano Ribeiro.

articles.title: Deputados criticam LOA com menos recursos para educação; governo nega | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto da Lei Orçamentária Anual (LOA) de 2027 foi enviado à Aleac ainda em maio, e voltou a ser analisado. Executivo afirma ainda que, na verdade, investimento vai aumentar.
articles.summary: Projeto da Lei Orçamentária Anual (LOA) de 2027 foi enviado à Aleac, onde ainda passará pelas comissões. Executivo estadual afirma ainda que, na verdade, investimento vai aumentar.
articles.body:
Deputados estaduais de oposição criticaram o projeto da Lei Orçamentária Anual (LOA) de 2027, enviado pelo Governo do Acre à Assembleia Legislativa do Acre (Aleac) por prever um total de 2.595.663.959,23 em recursos para a educação, cerca de 16,43% menor que o previsto para este ano, que é de R$ 3.106.291.635,02 .

Os parlamentares classificaram o montante como um corte de investimentos no setor, o que o governo negou por meio de nota. Membros da base do governo ainda não comentaram o assunto em plenário.

Conforme apurado pelo g1 , o projeto também prevê orçamento menor que em 2026 para outras sete áreas. A matéria foi enviada pela governadora Mailza Assis (PP) ainda em maio, e começou analisada em setembro. Ainda estão previstas discussões nas comissões legislativas e não há data definida para a votação.

No caso da educação, entretanto, o executivo estadual alegou que o que houve, na verdade, foi uma reclassificação das despesas com aposentados e pensionistas, que passaram a integrar a função Previdência Social.

"A mudança tem caráter exclusivamente orçamentário e busca assegurar maior transparência na apresentação das despesas públicas, distinguindo os recursos destinados às políticas educacionais daqueles relacionados às obrigações previdenciárias do Estado", justificou a Secretaria Estadual de Educação (SEE-AC).

O deputado estadual Tadeu Hassem (Republicanos) lamentou a diferença de valores. “É impensável e inegociável a redução dos investimentos na educação no ano de 2027. Eu acredito até que talvez seja um erro, um equívoco, que pode ter reparação. Porque a educação, os investimentos sempre são uma crescente, e cortar meio bilhão de reais da peça orçamentária é inegociável”, ponderou.

Segundo Edvaldo Magalhães (PCdoB), a Aleac vai buscar articulação para que este trecho do orçamento seja revisto.

"Nós vamos precisar abrir a porta do diálogo, sentar na mesa do entendimento e ter uma peça orçamentária que represente a realidade das finanças. Os problemas fiscais que o Acre está enfrentando não se resolvem subestimando o orçamento", criticou.

Em dezembro do ano passado, a LOA de 2026 foi aprovada com previsão de recursos de mais de R$ 13,8 bilhões, o que representou um aumento de mais de 14% em relação ao orçamento deste ano.

Já para o ano que vem, o projeto indica R$ 14.688.184.488,09, 6,30% maior que a de 2026.

O governo do Estado, por meio da Secretaria de Estado de Educação e Cultura (SEE), esclarece que não houve corte de recursos destinados à Educação na proposta orçamentária para 2027. A diferença de aproximadamente R$ 510 milhões apontada na comparação com 2026 decorre de uma reclassificação das despesas com aposentados e pensionistas, que passaram a integrar a função Previdência Social, conforme as normas de classificação orçamentária.

Para 2027, a proposta prevê um aumento de R$ 142,73 milhões, equivalente a 5,82%, no orçamento da Secretaria de Educação. A mudança tem caráter exclusivamente orçamentário e busca assegurar maior transparência na apresentação das despesas públicas, distinguindo os recursos destinados às políticas educacionais daqueles relacionados às obrigações previdenciárias do Estado.

articles.title: Maria Bethânia lança o álbum ao vivo do show dos 60 anos de carreira | G1
articles.body:
Maria Bethânia na casa Vivo Rio, em 17 de janeiro, primeiro dos dois dias de gravação do show '60 anos de carreira' na cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ) — Foto: Rodrigo Goffredo

♬ O álbum ao vivo com o registro do show comemorativo dos 60 anos de carreira de Maria Bethânia já tem data de lançamento.

Antecedido em 8 de outubro pelo single triplo que apresentou as gravações das músicas “Diz que fui por aí” (Zé Kétti e Hortênsio Rocha, 1964), “Mares da Espanha” (Angela Ro Ro, 1979) e “Palavras de Rita” (Rita Lee e Roberto de Carvalho, 2025), o álbum chegará aos plataformas de áudio na sexta-feira da próxima semana, 6 de novembro, em edição da gravadora Biscoito Fino.

Contudo, o registro audiovisual do show somente ficará disponível quatro dias depois, em 10 de novembro, no canal oficial da gravadora no YouTube.

Estreado pela cantora em setembro de 2025, o show “60 anos de carreira” teve imagem e som gravados em 17 e 18 de janeiro deste ano de 2026 em duas apresentações na casa Vivo Rio, na cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ).

Na ocasião da gravação, Bethânia já tinha feito alterações significativas no show, tirando as músicas “Gás neon” (Gonzaguinha, 1974) e “Eu mais ela” (Chico César, 2025) do roteiro e pondo “Olhos nos olhos” (Chico Buarque, 1976) no lugar de “Mar e lua” (Chico Buarque, 1980).

articles.title: Boney Kapoor was paid for the hair transplant reveal Janhvi Kapoor, Arjun Kapoor on 'Koffee With Karan', Varun Dhawan says his hair looks amazing
articles.summary: Boney Kapoor’s hair transformation became a talking point in 2024 after the film producer underwent a hair transplant.
articles.body: Boney Kapoor’s hair transformation became a talking point in 2024 after the film producer underwent a hair transplant. Now, his children, Janhvi Kapoor and Arjun Kapoor, have shared an interesting revelation about the procedure, claiming that their father was paid to get it done.The disclosure came during the latest episode of ‘Koffee With Karan’, when host Karan Johar asked Janhvi to share an entertaining rumour about her father that she would like to spread as part of the rapid-fire round.Janhvi was quick to respond, joking, “That he didn’t get a hair transplant done. And he grew his hair by concentrating.” Her brother Arjun burst out laughing before adding, “But if you roam around, you wouldn’t believe it.”Janhvi then asked Arjun, “Have you seen dad’s banners?” To this, he replied, “That’s called marketing.”Karan Johar soon brought up Boney’s makeover, saying, “I forgot to talk about Boney Ji’s makeover.” This prompted Janhvi to reveal, “Can I tell you that he has been paid to get a hair transplant?” A surprised Karan asked, “What, he got paid?” Both Janhvi and Arjun confirmed that it was true.Clarifying what she meant, Janhvi added, “He has not paid to get a hair transplant. He has gotten paid.” Varun Dhawan, who was also present during the conversation, praised the producer, saying, “But his hair looks amazing.”Karan, still taken aback by the revelation, asked, “So he is paid, that’s why he is smashed all over the city?” The siblings once again confirmed his assumption.Janhvi also revealed that more promotional banners featuring her father were in the pipeline. “There are more coming. I have got an approval of five more banners of him looking in the mirror without hair, sad, and with hair, happy,” she said, leaving the others laughing.Boney first drew attention to his hair transformation in 2024, when he travelled to Hyderabad for the inauguration of a hair transplant clinic. A video of the producer discussing his procedure subsequently surfaced online, in which he spoke about Eugenix and its role in his hair transplant.He later opened up about his decision to undergo the procedure, along with his weight-loss journey. Speaking at a press conference organised by the clinic, Boney recalled how his late wife, Sridevi, had encouraged him to lose weight before addressing his hair loss.

articles.title: 'Lioness' star Jill Wagner raises daughters in Tennessee town of 800, where horses and buggies still roam
articles.summary: "A Very Arctic Christmas" and "Lioness" star Jill Wagner traded Hollywood for a Tennessee town of 800, where Mennonites ride horses and buggies.
articles.body: From the high-stakes action of "Lioness" to the holiday adventure of "A Very Arctic Christmas," Jill Wagner is taking on two very different worlds. But off camera, the actress has traded Hollywood's hustle for a quieter life raising her two daughters on a Tennessee farm in a town of just 800 people — where horses and buggies are still a familiar sight. "First of all, I love Tennessee … I'm from the South. I'm from North Carolina," she told Fox News Digital. "I love the people here but especially love the small-town mentality." 'RANSOM CANYON' STAR JOSH DUHAMEL SAYS HE'D RATHER PUT MONEY INTO NORTH DAKOTA AFTER SELLING LOS ANGELES HOME Life in her Tennessee town offers a glimpse of a world that can feel far removed from Hollywood. "I was at the post office this morning and one of the Mennonites was in front of me … I got to look at their horse and buggy," she said. Wagner said the small-town atmosphere has become an important part of the childhood she and her husband want to give their girls. The actress explained why she hopes her daughters will eventually appreciate the slower pace, even if they someday follow in her footsteps and move to bigger cities. WATCH: JILL WAGNER TRADES HOLLYWOOD HUSTLE FOR TENNESSEE FAMILY LIFE "In some ways, going back to a simpler, slower pace … I think as we get older, or at least I know I can speak for myself, as I get older, I really value that," she added. Wagner knows the pull of Hollywood firsthand. She left home at 17 to pursue a career in entertainment and suspects her daughters may one day be eager to spread their own wings. But she hopes they'll always remember what their upbringing gave them. ‘SOPRANOS’ STAR JAMIE-LYNN SIGLER FLED HOLLYWOOD FOR TEXAS WHERE SHE NO LONGER FEELS ‘WATCHED’ "And I'm sure they'll do the same, but I hope what it does is bring them back to the simple-ness of life and what it can be … That's a gift that my husband and I gave them, and they probably don't even know it yet," she said. Away from the action of "Lioness," Wagner is embracing the holiday spirit in "A Very Arctic Christmas," reuniting with Cameron Mathison for a festive adventure. Wagner plays Jane, a wildlife conservationist who helps a father and daughter navigate an unexpected Arctic adventure after their holiday cruise goes off course. The actress said working with Mathison brings plenty of laughs to "A Very Arctic Christmas" set. "There's never any dull moment when you have Cameron Mathison and I on set together. In fact, it's hard for us to get through a scene without laughing, I'm sure. Robin Dunne, the director, is always rolling his eyes, like, ‘Oh, guys, guys, guys, guys, bring it in,'" she laughed. WATCH: JILL WAGNER DISHES ON THE ON-SET CHAOS WITH CO-STAR CAMERON MATHISON For Wagner, the holiday films also have a personal connection. The actress has found ways to include her daughters in her Christmas-movie tradition. When Wagner's daughters were younger, she included them in one of her films as extras, giving them a chance to sit on Santa's lap. Now that they're older, Wagner said they understand that Christmas movies are a genre of their own — and she hopes the experience becomes a lasting family tradition. "And I just hope that one day when I'm long and gone, that is a tradition with each other's families is that they get on Christmas, and they get to watch that movie and just kind of laugh at the fact that we're all in a movie together at Christmas," she added. While Wagner's career continues to take her between intense action roles and feel-good holiday projects, she values sharing those experiences with her daughters while giving them a childhood rooted in small-town life. When Fox News Digital asked whether her daughters were becoming the Tennessee farm girls she had envisioned, Wagner admitted there's still some work to do. "So, I don't know about farm girl. I know that … they love outdoors. They don't necessarily like doing farm work. So, we're trying to still work on that," she laughed. "They do love running around barefooted in the dirt, and they can play outside all day long, which I love for them," Wagner said. The family hopes to add chickens and goats when Wagner's work schedule allows more time at home. "Maybe one day we'll get a horse or a pony for them," she added. articles.title: BJP MP Manoj Tiwari swims in Yamuna to give ‘clean’ message
articles.summary: BJP MP Manoj Tiwari swims in Yamuna ahead of Chhath, citing cleanup work; AAP disputes claims as DPCC data shows high pollution downstream.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ahead of Chhath Puja, BJP MP Manoj Tiwari Thursday took a dip and swam in the Yamuna at Sonia Vihar, praising the work undertaken to clean the river under the leadership of CM Rekha Gupta.Tiwari, who represents North East Delhi, said he was “overjoyed” the work had made it possible for him to enter the river. He credited PM Modi and Gupta, saying the objective was to provide a clean Yamuna to Delhi residents.“How can we not appreciate the work that has been done here? I will tell Arvind Kejriwal that this is all a sign of cleanliness. There might be crocodiles in the water here, but crocodiles come in clean water,” Tiwari said, adding his visit was intended to send a message, not aimed at shaming Kejriwal.Responding to Tiwari, AAP said its karyakartas had visited the Yamuna and exposed BJP’s false claims. According to a party worker, the water at the site was black and heavily polluted. The workers said Tiwari had taken a dip during the Yamuna Ghat cleaning drive and his claim that he was drinking the river water was “completely false”.AAP alleged Tiwari was from Purvanchal and was “staging theatrics” as Chhath was approaching. Issuing an open challenge to him, it said, “Take a dip where the drain water flows into the Yamuna, drink the water and livestream the entire exercise for the public across all your social media accounts. People elected Manoj Tiwari as their MP because they trusted him, but he is trying to mislead the people of Delhi.”As per DPCC’s latest report for Sept, the monsoon rain received by Delhi this year failed to improve Yamuna’s water quality. Several monitoring points recorded higher pollution in Sept 2026 than Sept 2025. While river stretch between Palla where it enters the city and Wazirabad barrage, where Tiwari took the dip, is comparatively cleaner and within standards, its downstream Wazirabad barrage, post the confluence of Najafgarh drain, is heavily polluted.The DPCC report said at Palla, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) is 2mg/l, dissolved oxygen 6.5mg/l and fecal coliform 1,100 MPN/100ml -- all within standards. However, downstream Wazirabad, at ISBT Bridge, the Sept 7 sample recorded BOD of 30 mg/l, compared with 8 mg/l on Sept 3 last year. Chemical oxygen demand (COD) rose from 44 mg/l to 92 mg/l over the same period. The fecal coliform count increased from 2,800 to 35,000. At ITO Bridge, BOD climbed from 4 mg/l to 18 mg/l, while COD rose from 20 mg/l to 60 mg/l. Fecal coliform levels increased from 1,800 to 17,000 MPN/100 ml.A BOD limit of 3 mg/l or less and dissolved oxygen of at least 5 mg/l are specified for bathing. For fecal coliform, the desirable limit is 500 MPN/100 ml, with 2,500 MPN/100 ml as the maximum permissible level.During festivals like Chhath, stretch between Palla and Wazirabad gets a booster of fresh water from Hathini Kund barrage, flushing the pollutants out. However, the stretch is not immune to pollution. In Oct second week, visuals of hundreds of dead fish and many more gasping for oxygen in Yamuna upstream of Wazirabad raised fresh concerns over the river’s pollution levels. Experts held industrial effluents from Haryana responsible for that.The Yamuna’s condition becomes a major political flashpoint every year ahead of Chhath, when devotees enter the river for rituals amid concerns over sewage pollution and toxic foam. articles.summary: La televisiva comentó que no entiende cómo Atocha no sabía que hubiera un tren parado durante 15’ en las vías antes de la colisión
articles.body: Este miércoles, 28 de octubre, en Urda (Toledo) un tren de alta velocidad (AVE) de Renfe impactó con uno de Iryo que estaba detenido. El accidente deja 69 muertos y varias decenas de fallecidos. Tras el suceso, Óscar Puente, ministro de Transportes, compareció para comunicar la información que tenía al respecto. Puente indicó que seis trenes se detuvieron en la ruta de Madrid-Andalucía tras fallar el sistema de seguridad LZB. A partir de ahí, la gestión pasó al centro de control de Atocha, que se encargó de indicar los próximos pasos a seguir. Sobre las 8:31 horas, el maquinista del AVE comunicó que se había “caído” la central de Urda, en referencia al sistema LZB. Desde Madrid le comentaron que desconectarse y volviera a conectar el LZB y reanudase la marcha al amparo del BSL de manera “normal”. Por otro lado, a las 8;41 horas, el Iryo contactó con Atocha, comentando que estaban parados en la entrada de Urda, varios kilómetros delante del AVE. La respuesta desde Atocha fue la siguiente: “Desconecte y vuelva a conectar el sistema LZB para reanudar la marcha al amparo del BSL con marcha normal”. A las 8:48 horas tuvo lugar la última conversación y la maquinista de Iryo insistió en que no podía revisar el sistema LZB y que seguía detenida. El controlador de Adif le comentó que volviera a llamar si tenía algún problema. Tan solo seis minutos después, a las 8:54 horas, tuvo lugar el fatal desenlace. En este contexto, las opiniones siguen llegando. articles.title: Halle Berry loses custody to ex Olivier Martinez amid abuse allegations
articles.summary: Halle Berry will remain without primary custody of the 13-year-old son she shares with ex Olivier Martinez, who accused the actress of physical abuse.
articles.body:
Halle Berry will remain without primary custody of her 13-year-old son.

A decision has been made in the ongoing legal battle between the actress, 60, and her ex Olivier Martinez after he accused her of physically abusing their son Maceo. On Thursday, Oct, 29, Los Angeles Superior Court judge Shelley Kaufman dismissed Martinez's request for a domestic violence restraining order, but denied Berry's requests for 50/50 custody and overnight visits, according court documents obtained by NBCLA .

The former couple, who split in 2015 after two years of marriage, previously shared joint custody until Martinez, 60, was granted a temporary restraining order earlier this month. At the time, the French actor cited an incident on Sept. 26, during which Berry allegedly "attacked" Maceo by "jumping on him, putting her hands around his neck, and choking him," per documents obtained by USA TODAY.

Halle Berry's life in the spotlight – Photos of her highlights

Martinez further alleged several prior instances of abuse involving the teen and sought sole legal and physical custody. While Kaufman ultimately rejected a permanent domestic violence restraining order, she ruled that the custody arrangement from the TRO would stay in place pending additional proceedings.

This leaves Berry, who denies all allegations, with joint legal custody, but limited physical custody of Maceo.

In a statement to USA TODAY after the Oct. 29 ruling, Berry's attorney, Marina Beck, said, "We are extremely pleased that the Court has dissolved the TRO. As we move forward, Halle is determined to continue to focus on the well-being and best interests of her family."

Martinez's lawyer, Patrick Baghdaserians, told TMZ that his client having primary physical custody is a "huge victory."

USA TODAY has reached out to lawyers for Berry and Martinez for comment.

Berry's attorney Beck previously addressed Martinez's allegations in an Oct. 1 statement to USA TODAY. Calling Martinez's filing "entirely meritless and deliberately misleading," Beck said there is extensive evidence, including previous court rulings, that Berry's ex repeatedly violated court orders, interfered with their son's therapeutic and educational care and alleged he has been legally sanctioned for his conduct."In a way, today's filing is not entirely unexpected from an individual with a well-documented history of erratic, possessive and violent behavior," Beck said. "Fortunately, Halle is used to this kind of outrageous conduct from Mr. Martinez and, while she is deeply saddened, she will not allow it to deter her from fighting for Maceo's best interests and providing him with the love and support he needs."

Berry and Martinez married in July 2013 and welcomed Maceo later that same year. They filed for divorce in 2015 and it was finalized in 2023 after an eight-year legal battle, with both agreeing to joint legal and physical custody of their son Maceo and for Martinez to receive $8,000 a month in child support.

Halle Berry's daughter spoke out in support of her mom

The "Catwoman" star also shares 18-year-old daughter Nahla Aubry with ex-boyfriend Gabriel Aubry. Nahla Aubry submitted a written declaration on Oct. 3 in support of her mom, in which she told the court she was "shocked, very sad, and very upset" by Martinez's claims.

"Having lived with my mom my entire life and having personally observed her relationship with Maceo for years, the allegations are completely inconsistent with the mom I know," Aubry wrote, calling Berry "a loving and devoted parent" who has "has always encouraged" both her and her brother "to maintain loving relationships with our fathers."

Aubry accused Martinez of being on "quest to destroy my mom" and said she is "heartbroken" to see Maceo "become the subject of a public dispute that he may not fully understand."

"Based on my observations throughout Maceo's life, I believe he loves our mom very much and shares a close bond with her. I have seen him hug her, kiss her, tell her he loves her, seek her comfort, and enjoy spending time with her," Aubry's declaration read. "At the same time, I have also witnessed occasions when Maceo has been disrespectful, at times aggressive, and unwilling to follow rules at home."

She added, "When that occurred, my mom responded the same way she did with me when I was growing up: by enforcing appropriate boundaries and consequences, such as limiting screen time, imposing time-outs, or restricting access to electronics and play dates. I never observed anything abusive about her parenting."

articles.title: Patrick Stewart, actor known for iconic roles in ‘Star Trek’ and ‘X-Men,’ dies at 86
articles.summary: The beloved star of the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises died Wednesday following diagnoses of Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.
articles.body: Beloved actor Patrick Stewart has died following a diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, his representative confirmed. He was 86. “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” Kelly Bush Novak, his longtime spokesperson, said in a statement Thursday. Stewart — whose storied career included the iconic roles of Professor X in the “X-Men” film series and Capt. Jean-Luc Picard in the “Star Trek” franchise — had spent quality time with loved ones before his death, according to the statement. “He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” the statement said. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection of his invincible grace.” Stewart, an indelible part of the “Star Trek” legacy, played Jean-Luc Picard for seven seasons on “Star Trek: The Next Generation,” from 1987 to 1994, and in multiple films, and he reprised the role in the Paramount+ show “Star Trek: Picard,” from 2020 to 2023. He stepped into the role of Professor Charles Xavier with the 2000 film “X-Men” and continued to depict the genius mutant telepath in multiple sequels. He was featured in a trailer for the highly anticipated “Avengers: Doomsday” film scheduled to be released in December, reprising the role for the eighth time in the mega Marvel crossover. He had most recently done voice-over work in the film “The Sheep Detectives” and appeared in the Prime Video series “Bait,” both in 2026, according to his IMDb profile. Born in the town of Mirfield in West Yorkshire, England, he joined the acclaimed Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966. He went on to make his Broadway debut in 1971 in “A Midsummer Night’s Dream” and forged a career on the silver screen. In his theater career, he graced numerous Broadway and West End stages — including as the title character in “Macbeth” on Broadway, for which he was nominated for a Tony in 2008. Across the pond, he won two Laurence Olivier Awards focused on London theater: the first in 1979 for best actor in a supporting role for his role in “Antony and Cleopatra” and the second in 2009 for best performance in a supporting role as King Claudius in “Hamlet.” As a voice actor, Stewart lent his commanding baritone to the character Avery Bullock, the eccentric CIA director on the animated comedy “American Dad,” from its 2005 debut through this year. He also voiced several characters, including his own Capt. Jean-Luc Picard, on the animated comedy “Family Guy” from 2005 to 2018. “His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the statement from Novak, Stewart’s spokesperson, said. “He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.” Off the stage, he was dedicated to philanthropy and activism, including advocating for human rights, domestic violence survivors, refugees, veteran mental health services and animal welfare. A revered figure in Hollywood — with myriad accolades spanning nominations for Emmy Awards, Golden Globes and Screen Actors Guild Awards — he was also knighted in 2010 by Queen Elizabeth II for his services to drama. The statement closed with a quote from his 2023 book, “Making It So: A Memoir”: “Like me, Jean-Luc has lived an unusual life that has taken him far beyond the bounds of normal human experience. But he is also someone who has remained true to his earthbound roots, for they are what gave him his identity. In the end, he feels the call of home, as do I.” Marvel Studios said in a statement that it is “deeply saddened” by Stewart’s passing. “Sir Patrick brought Professor Charles Xavier to life with extraordinary grace, intelligence, and humanity, defining the character for generations of fans, from ‘X-Men’ to ‘Logan’ to ‘Avengers: Doomsday,’” the statement said. “He was a singular talent, a generous collaborator, and a true gentleman. Our hearts go out to his wife Sunny, his children, his friends, and the countless fans around the world whose lives he touched with his art.” Kevin Feige, president of Marvel Studios, recalled first seeing Stewart in action. “I’ll never forget the first time I saw Sir Patrick Stewart on the set of the first X-Men. After years of knowing him as the inimitable Captain Picard, I was in awe — and he turned out to be everything I had seen on screen and more: brilliant, charming, warm, generous, with a quiet strength and gravitas,” Feige said in a statement. “Away from the cameras, he was even more remarkable, with a wonderfully sharp sense of humor. It was a true privilege to know him and to work with him. His legacy lives on not only in decades of extraordinary work, but in the many, many people he mentored. He will be deeply missed,” he added. The Royal Shakespeare Company hailed Stewart as “a colossus of both stage and screen and one of the finest classical Shakespearean actors of his generation.” “Despite being one of the most recognizable Shakespearean performers in the world, Sir Patrick remained deeply connected to Stratford-upon-Avon and the RSC throughout his career,” the company said, referring to Shakespeare’s birthplace, where RSC is based. “His contribution to our company and to our industry is beyond measure.” The company said Stewart served as a core member through 1982. Tributes poured in for Stewart from devoted fans and co-stars. Hugh Jackman, who played Wolverine to Stewart’s Professor X in the “X-Men” films, shared photos of the pair on Instagram, writing: “We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days.” William Shatner, a fellow “Star Trek” captain, remembered Stewart as “a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor.” “From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work,” he said on social media. Jonathan Frakes, who played Cmdr. William Riker in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and in “Star Trek: Picard,” wrote on his Instagram Story: “Rest in peace my friend.” “Star Trek: Picard” executive producer Akiva Goldsman remembered Stewart as “not only a true lion of the profession, he was the rarest of alchemists, one who could literally turn the written word into flesh and blood.” “Patrick was kind, strong, fiercely intelligent, collaborative, vulnerable and wise. His Captain Jean-Luc Picard permanently expanded the universe of Star Trek without measure. He will be deeply missed by this one fan and by so many more,” Goldsman said in a statement.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart, legendary 'Star Trek' and 'X-Men' actor, dies at 86
articles.summary: Legendary "Star Trek" and "X-Men" actor Patrick Stewart died at his Los Angeles home at 86 following a battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia.
articles.body: Sir Patrick Stewart, the legendary British actor best known for portraying Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek" and Professor Charles Xavier in the "X-Men" franchise, has died at 86, according to a statement shared on his Instagram account. Stewart died Wednesday at his Los Angeles home, surrounded by family and friends and cared for by his wife, Sunny, following a battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, the statement said. "We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia," Stewart's longtime spokeswoman Kelly Bush Novak said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all. We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace."She added that he went from his home in Yorkshire to the Royal Shakespeare Company and on to an "equally acclaimed career spanning six decades on Broadway, the silver screen and television." PATRICK STEWART: A LIFE IN PICTURES "His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre," she wrote. "He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise." HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026: PHOTOSBush Novak said that Stewart's professional accomplishments were "humbly matched by his philanthropy and activism on behalf of human rights, survivors of domestic violence, global refugees, veterans’ mental health services, and animal welfare, particularly his cherished foster pitties. He was a Knight, Chancellor, motor sport enthusiast, and lifelong Huddersfield Football fan. He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role — in his art and life." ‘STAR TREK’ STAR PATRICK STEWART RECALLS VIOLENT CHILDHOOD WITH BRITISH ARMY FATHER While Stewart was best known for his TV and film sci-fi roles, he was a prolific — and classically trained theater actor. Stewart was first discovered for the part of Jean-Luc Picard by a "Star Trek: The Next Generation" producer when he was reading Shakespeare at a UCLA lecture. PATRICK STEWART CONFIRMS 'STAR TREK' RETURN AS JEAN-LUC PICARD The actor didn't expect the series, which revamped the original "Star Trek" starring William Shatner, to go past one season. "I was very naïve about the conditions attached to series television in the U.S.A.," Stewart admitted to Startrek.com in 2010, explaining he found out he had to sign a six-year contract for the series. "Every single person I spoke to – agents, directors, screenwriters, other actors – said, ‘Oh, don’t worry about six years. You’ll be lucky to make it through the first year.’ Everybody felt it was madness to try to revive an iconic series like William Shatner and Leonard Nimoy’s Star Trek. So, on the basis of that advice I signed the six-year contract." The series ended up running for seven seasons and spawned four films: "Star Trek: Generations," "Star Trek: First Contact," "Star Trek: Insurrection," and "Star Trek: Nemesis." Shatner paid tribute to Stewart on Thursday afternoon. "What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor," Shatner wrote. "From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work. My heart goes out to Sunny and his family. He will be deeply missed." His "X-Men co-star Hugh Jackman wrote on X: "We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days." "Star Trek" star George Takei wrote on X that fans "across the world" were mourning the loss of a "true and irreplaceable legend. As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, Patrick Stewart took the starship Enterprise to places it had never gone before. He inspired a whole next generation of star-gazers who looked longingly ahead to a brighter future for all humanity. Our hearts are heavy, indeed. Rest in the heavens, Captain." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Despite becoming one of the most iconic faces of the "Star Trek" universe and taking on the part of Professor Charles Xavier in nine films, starting with "X-Men" in 2000, Stewart largely avoided becoming typecast as he said he feared. He was cast in 1991's "L.A. Story," "Robin Hood: Men in Tights," "Conspiracy Theory," the TV miniseries "Moby Dick," "A Christmas Carol," "A Lion in Winter," "Extras," a 2009 TV movie of "Hamlet" in which he played Claudius, and Seth MacFarlane comedies "Blunt Talk" and "American Dad." Stewart even voiced one of the sheep in Amazon's "The Sheep Detectives," which came out earlier this year. He most recently repriced his "Star Trek" role in 2020 for a three-season run on "Star Trek: Picard" for Paramount+. MacFarlane paid tribute to Stewart on his Instagram on Thursday, writing that he "grew up as a fan, and was later gifted the privilege of becoming a colleague and friend, working with him for many years on ‘American Dad!’, ‘Family Guy’, and ‘Ted’. He was that rare actor who could take any bit of dialogue and elevate it, making a good writer sound great, and a great writer sound masterful. He was also as humble as they come. I remember exchanging emails with him a number of years ago when he was beginning day 1 of a new film. He commented to me that he always walked onto a new set feeling like the biggest novice there. My stunned reaction was the same as anyone’s would be. I said, ‘Patrick, if you feel that way, the rest of us are screwed.’ We have lost a legendary actor today, and for many of us, a good friend. He will be deeply missed by the entire planet." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? On stage, Stewart played Claudius, Ebenezer Scrooge and received his only Tony nomination for his starring role in "Macbeth" on Broadway, following a run in London's West End. I memorized all the soliloquies just because I thought they were great. And they stuck, so I didn’t have to learn those bits of the play, which is a blessing, because learning lines has now become the one curse of this job." articles.body: Sir Patrick Stewart, the acclaimed British actor celebrated for his performances on stage and his iconic roles in Star Trek: The Next Generation and the X-Men franchise, has died at the age of 86. The actor passed away at his home in Los Angeles on October 28, 2026, following a battle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.A statement shared on Instagram on Thursday, October 29, announced his death, saying he had been surrounded by his family and friends during his final hours.“We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement read.“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” it continued. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection of his invincible grace.”The family has requested that, instead of flowers, memorial contributions be made to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America’s caregiver resources.Sir Patrick Stewart’s six-decade career in theatre and cinemaStewart leaves behind a remarkable career spanning more than six decades, establishing himself as one of Britain’s most distinguished stage and screen actors. His accolades included two Olivier Awards and a Grammy Award, alongside nominations for a Tony Award, three Golden Globes, four Emmy Awards and three Screen Actors Guild Awards.In 2010, Queen Elizabeth II knighted him for his services to drama, recognising his contribution to British theatre and international entertainment.His professional career gained momentum in 1966 when he joined the Royal Shakespeare Company. During his years with the company, he built a reputation as a formidable classical actor, performing Shakespeare alongside some of the leading names in British theatre, including Sir Ian McKellen and Dame Judi Dench.Stewart made his Broadway debut in 1971 in a production of A Midsummer Night’s Dream. Although international audiences would eventually associate him with science fiction and superhero films, theatre remained a constant throughout his life.From Captain Jean-Luc Picard to Professor Charles XavierStewart became a global star in 1987 when he was cast as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation. His portrayal of the thoughtful, principled starship captain became one of the defining performances of the franchise.The series ran until 1994, and Stewart subsequently reprised Picard in several Star Trek films, including Star Trek: Generations, Star Trek: First Contact, Star Trek: Insurrection and Star Trek: Nemesis. He returned to the role decades later in Star Trek: Picard, which followed the character in his later years.He reached another generation of moviegoers through the X-Men franchise, playing Professor Charles Xavier, the powerful telepath and mentor to a group of mutants. His performance brought warmth, authority and moral complexity to the character, making him a central figure in the superhero film series.Despite his success in Hollywood, Stewart continued to return to the stage, demonstrating his enduring commitment to classical theatre.His love for theatre never fadedIn 2008, Stewart appeared in Hamlet, playing King Claudius in a production that moved from London’s West End to Broadway. His performance earned him his second Olivier Award and further recognition in the theatre world.His stage work also included acclaimed productions of Samuel Beckett’s Waiting for Godot and Harold Pinter’s No Man’s Land, in which he performed alongside longtime friend Sir Ian McKellen.Stewart’s ability to move between Shakespearean drama, science fiction and mainstream cinema made him a distinctive presence across several generations of entertainment. His deep, resonant voice and commanding screen presence became trademarks of his performances.Sir Patrick Stewart’s marriages and family lifeStewart was married three times during his life. He married Sheila Falconer in 1966, and the couple had two children, Daniel and Sophia. Their marriage ended in divorce in 1990.In 2000, he married Wendy Neuss, a television producer associated with Star Trek: The Next Generation. They divorced in 2003.In 2008, Stewart began dating American singer-songwriter Sunny Ozell. The couple married in September 2013 in Nevada, with McKellen officiating at their wedding.Stewart later revealed that the couple had actually held an earlier, private ceremony at a Mexican restaurant in Los Angeles after discovering that McKellen’s credentials were not valid in Nevada. The story became a memorable anecdote about the actor’s friendship with McKellen and his personal life.A lasting legacy on stage and screenStewart’s death marks the end of an extraordinary chapter in British acting, but his performances are likely to remain familiar to audiences for years to come. From Shakespearean characters to Captain Picard and Professor Xavier, he brought a distinctive combination of intelligence, gravitas and humanity to his roles.His career demonstrated that classical theatre and popular entertainment could coexist, allowing a highly trained stage actor to become a household name across the world. His work in Star Trek helped define a generation of science fiction television, while his contribution to the X-Men films made him an enduring part of modern superhero cinema.As tributes emerge following his death, Stewart is being remembered not only for the characters he portrayed but also for a lifetime devoted to his craft. articles.body:
Donald Trump 's recent comments about rapper Nicki Minaj at a Michigan rally may have greatly affected his wife, Melania Trump .

A psychologist revealed that the president praising Nicki's body and asking her to stand up for the crowd may signal a "clear issue of disrespect" for Melania, who wasn't present at the rally.

Donald Trump has been noted to repeatedly make jokes and comments that critics say come at Melania Trump's expense, and the latest has drawn more attention to how she handles the public statements.

T rump's Shocking Remark About Female Rapper Could Have 'Consequences' For Melania

Speaking to Irish Star , Clinical psychologist Dr Tracy King observed that Trump "essentially objectified Nicki for the point of entertainment," which could impact Melania, especially because of the very public nature of the moment.

"For a wife watching this, there is a clear issue of disrespect. Trump himself was aware he could have caused offense to Nicki Minaj, noted it, and then minimized it," King stated.

She explained that Trump gave no consideration for Melania as to how his words could affect her and that the "hurt" the first lady may feel is nothing as simple as "jealousy."

"He did not openly consider his wife. Yet his words have consequences for her… There is a lack of consideration here that will contribute to a lack of trust," the psychologist explained.

According to Dr. King, respect or lack of it is clear in how one partner behaves when the other is "present and when they are not."

She added that Trump's remarks could lead people to question Melania's self-respect as she remains in a marriage where her husband publicly disrespects her.

"Melania will also know that others will see it and make lots of assumptions about her self-respect, as she is in a marriage where she is treated this way," she said.

Expert Warns The 'Embarrassment' Could Be Lasting For The First Lady

King also pointed out that the public nature of the moment worsens the situation for Melania, as a private inappropriate moment is "something a couple can control in terms of who knows about it and how they address it."

She suggests that as the remarks were made in a public forum, "feelings of embarrassment and shame" are likely to re-emerge as clips of the moments go viral and comments about it persist.

The expert warns that the moment could repeatedly make headlines, constantly renewing attention on Melania, making it difficult to move on from what she may have perceived as disrespectful.

However, King acknowledged that Melania may be unbothered by the remarks but suggested that an indifferent reaction could signal that there is emotional distance and a "huge rupture" in the first marriage.

"If anger is felt, a person is still trying to be heard and set a boundary. If this is gone, hope is gone," she concluded.

The first lady showed "nonverbal avoidance" of intimacy with Trump during an awkward kiss.

Donald Trump Praised Nicki Minaj's 'Beautiful' Derriere At Michigan Rally

According to a report by The Guardian , during a rally in support of Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, Trump singled out Nicki and made the comments that have sparked some controversy.

"By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before – Nicki Minaj," he said, noting multiple times that the "Anaconda" rapper's rear end was "hard to miss."

"OK, I'm going to get back to my story, Nicki. I hope Nicki wasn't insulted, but we love Nicki. She's been with us for a long time," the 80-year-old added.

Minaj, in her gold Gucci suit, came out in support of Trump and led chants of the name of the president and that of Republican candidates.

She claimed that Americans needed all these "great people" elected before she left the stage, to which Trump remarked, "She never looked more beautiful. She gets it. She's smart."

A Pattern Of Jokes And Comments At Melania Trump's Expense

Dr. King's expert analysis comes as other experts have pointed out Trump's tendency to make jokes about Melania during political speeches that could be perceived as disrespectful.

As reported by HuffPost , following remarks by the president at a rally in Wasilla, Alaska, and Bullhead City, Arizona, Psychologist Greg Cason argued that there's "hostile humor" in Trump's Melania material.

He stated that "Recruiting the audience creates a power imbalance in that moment," and that Trump appeared to be using Melania for "material, not advice."

Marriage and family therapist Jennifer Chappell Marsh implied in her expert opinion that Trump making a joke at Melania's expense could leave her feeling "embarrassed and devalued."

She explained that such behavior persisting even after it had been addressed may indicate that there's "underlying resentment being expressed passive-aggressively through 'humor.'"

Relationship Expert Says Melania And Donald Trump's Marriage Is 'Not In A Healthy Place'

The relationship between the President and First Lady of the United States has drawn a lot of attention, especially as rumors swirl that they "barely speak" and that there's trouble in paradise.

In a previous Irish Star report, relationship expert Gemma Logan said that "a marriage where two people are reportedly barely speaking is clearly not in a healthy place."

She explained that if the rumors were true, it would suggest that Trump and Melania may not feel "emotionally connected" to each other even when they meet up and could lead to the pair living separate lives.

articles.title: Celine Dion was diagnosed with stiff person syndrome in 2022; it affected her ability to walk and sing, her foundation donated $2 million for research before her return to the stage in Paris
articles.summary: Celine Dion’s journey with stiff person syndrome has been marked by uncertainty, difficult health challenges and an unwavering determination to find a way
articles.body: Celine Dion’s journey with stiff person syndrome has been marked by uncertainty, difficult health challenges and an unwavering determination to find a way forward. The singer publicly revealed her diagnosis in December 2022, sharing that the rare neurological disorder had affected her ability to walk and sing. In June 2024, the Celine Dion Foundation announced a $2 million donation to the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus to support research into stiff person syndrome (SPS) and other autoimmune neurological conditions.The contribution was aimed at advancing scientific understanding of the disorder, improving diagnosis and treatment, and supporting patients living with the condition. It also established the Celine Dion Foundation Endowed Chair in Autoimmune Neurology, with Dr Amanda Piquet appointed as its inaugural chairholder.Celine Dion’s foundation donated $2 million to support researchAnnounced on June 18, 2024, the donation was intended to fund five years of research and clinical work at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus. The initiative focused on developing a better understanding of stiff person syndrome, improving early diagnosis and patient care, and supporting clinical trials that could lead to more effective therapies.Dr Amanda Piquet, associate professor of neurology at the University of Colorado School of Medicine and director of its Autoimmune Neurology Program, was named the inaugural holder of the endowed chair. She had also been treating Dion at UCHealth University of Colorado Hospital for two years.Speaking about the research initiative, Dr Piquet said, “This is just the start of a very bright future for those with the disease.” She also underlined the need for more effective treatment options, adding, “We need better therapies for patients. Ultimately, what we’d love is a cure.”The foundation’s contribution was significant not only because of the funding involved but also because it brought greater attention to a rare condition that can be difficult to recognise and diagnose.What is stiff person syndrome and how does it affect patients?Stiff person syndrome is a rare, chronic and progressive autoimmune neurological disorder that affects the central nervous system. It is characterised by muscle stiffness and rigidity, along with painful spasms that can affect movement and mobility. In severe cases, the condition can make everyday activities, including walking, difficult.For Dion, the symptoms also affected her ability to sing and perform. The singer had spoken about how the disorder interfered with her voice and her control over her body, forcing her to step away from live performances while she focused on her health.SPS can be particularly challenging to diagnose because its symptoms may resemble those of other neurological, muscular or psychological conditions. Some patients are initially diagnosed with conditions such as multiple sclerosis or fibromyalgia, which can delay the identification of the disorder. The diagnostic process can take years for some patients.The condition is also reported more frequently among women, with symptoms often emerging in adulthood. Greater awareness among medical professionals and more research into the disorder are considered important steps towards improving diagnosis and care.Is there a cure for stiff person syndrome?There is currently no known cure for stiff person syndrome. However, treatments can help manage symptoms and improve quality of life. These may include immunotherapies such as intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), along with muscle relaxants and medications that help control spasms.Supportive approaches, including physiotherapy and other forms of rehabilitation, may also help patients manage stiffness and mobility-related difficulties. Treatment, however, varies from person to person, depending on the severity of the condition and the symptoms experienced.Dion’s health journey was also documented in the Prime Video documentary I Am: Céline Dion, which premiered on June 25, 2024. The film offered an intimate look at the singer’s life with the disorder and the physical and emotional challenges she faced while trying to continue doing what she loved.Speaking to Vogue France in 2024, Dion expressed hope that scientific research would eventually lead to a breakthrough. “I hope that we find a miracle, a way to cure it with scientific research. But for now I have to learn to live with it,” she said.Celine Dion returns to the stage after six yearsAfter years away from live performances, Dion announced her return to the stage in an emotional video message broadcast beneath the Eiffel Tower on March 30, 2026, her birthday. She revealed plans for a limited engagement in Paris, with 10 performances scheduled at Paris La Défense Arena between September 12 and October 14, 2026.Reflecting on the support she had received during her health struggles, the singer said, “Over the last few years, every day that’s gone by, I’ve felt your prayers and support, your kindness and love. You’ve helped me in ways that I can’t even describe, and I’m truly fortunate to have your support.”She also described the announcement as the best birthday gift she could have hoped for. “This year, I’m getting the best birthday gift of my life…I’m getting the chance to see you, to perform for you once again in Paris, beginning in September! I’m feeling good, I’m strong, I’m feeling excited, obviously a little nervous, but most of all, I’m grateful to all of YOU! I love you all and I’ll see you soon!”Dion went on to return to the stage on September 12, 2026, marking her first live performance in six years. The opening night of her Celine Dion Paris 2026-2027 shows brought her back before a sold-out audience, turning the moment into a deeply emotional milestone for the singer and her fans.Addressing the audience, she said, “Finally, it’s amazing we are all together. I made a promise to come back and to be back on stage. So here I am, singing for you, singing for me, singing life.”After battling the condition for years, Celine Dion’s return to the stage marked an important chapter in her journey. While she continues to live with stiff person syndrome, the singer’s comeback was a moment of hope for her and her fans, who had been waiting to see her perform live again.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: Hollywood is mourning the loss of one of its most beloved screen legends - Sir Patrick Stewart.The actor, who captivated generations of viewers as the cerebral Captain Jean-Luc Picard in 'Star Trek: The Next Generation' and the telepathic Professor Charles Xavier in the 'X-Men' franchise, passed away on Wednesday. He was 86. The actor reportedly died at his Los Angeles home, following what his spokesperson described as a “brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to a statement shared on his X account.Soon after the news broke, tributes poured in from across the entertainment industry, with Hugh Jackman, William Shatner, the Russo Brothers and Marvel Studios among those honouring the veteran actor. Co-stars, colleagues and fans remembered Stewart's extraordinary legacy, celebrating a career that spanned decades and left an indelible mark on both television and cinema.Patrick Stewart's Marvel family mourns his demiseHugh Jackman, who co-starred with Patrick Stewart in 8 films over the years, primarily through the X-Men franchise and a 2026 comedy, paid poignant tribute to his late friend. Sharing photos from behind the scenes on the big stage and their time on the sets of 'Logan', he wrote, "We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days."Marvel Studios released a statement honouring his legacy that began with his stint in 'X-Men' and will reportedly conclude with his final turn in 'Avengers: Doomsday'. The statement read, “All of us at Marvel Studios are deeply saddened by the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart. Sir Patrick brought Professor Charles Xavier to life with extraordinary grace, intelligence, and humanity, defining the character for generations of fans, from X-Men to Logan to Avengers: Doomsday. He was a singular talent, a generous collaborator, and a true gentleman. Our hearts go out to his wife Sunny, his children, his friends, and the countless fans around the world whose lives he touched with his art.”'Avengers: Doomsday' director-duo the Russo Brothers also took to their handles to pay tribute. Sharing a still of Stewart from what is said to be his final film, they wrote, "We’ve been lucky enough to work with some of our childhood heroes. And Sir Patrick Stewart will always be one of them. A legendary actor with an unmistakeable presence, and an unmatched integrity. Thank you for entertaining all of us, sir. And for teaching us humanity, both on and off the screen. Sending our love to your family, friends, and fans around the world."Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige also paid tribute to Stewart in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter, he said, "Away from the cameras, he was even more remarkable, with a wonderfully sharp sense of humor. It was a true privilege to know him and to work with him. His legacy lives on not only in decades of extraordinary work, but in the many, many people he mentored. He will be deeply missed.”MacFarlane, who worked with Stewart on numerous projects, including Family Guy, Ted, Blunt Talk and American Dad!, penned a heartfelt note that read, "Patrick was one of those icons who we somehow all took for granted would always be with us.I grew up as a fan, and was later gifted the privilege of becoming a colleague and friend, working with him for many years on “American Dad!”, “Family Guy”, and “Ted”. He was that rare actor who could take any bit of dialogue and elevate it, making a good writer sound great, and a great writer sound masterful. He was also as humble as they come. I remember exchanging emails with him a number of years ago when he was beginning day 1 of a new film. He commented to me that he always walked onto a new set feeling like the biggest novice there. My stunned reaction was the same as anyone’s would be. I said, “Patrick, if you feel that way, the rest of us are screwed.” We have lost a legendary actor today, and for many of us, a good friend. He will be deeply missed by the entire planet."Star Trek family remembers Patrick StewartStewart's former co-star William Shatner, who played Captain James T. Kirk in 1994’s Star Trek: Generations, wrote in a statement on X, “What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor. From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work.”Star Trek: Discovery actor Wilson Cruz said an Instagram Story that he's been "devastated" by the news of Stewart's death, Stewart's Star Trek: The Next Generation costar Jonathan Frakes wrote on his own account, “Rest in peace my friend.”Jonathan Frakes, who played Commander William Riker in Star Trek: The Next Generation series with Stewart, took to his handle to write, "Rest in peace my friend"George Takei and Stewart’s fellow “Star Trek” alum, on social media, “Fans across the world mourn the passing of a true and irreplaceable legend. As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, Patrick Stewart took the starship Enterprise to places it had never gone before. He inspired a whole next generation of star-gazers who looked longingly ahead to a brighter future for all humanity. Our hearts are heavy, indeed. Rest in the heavens, Captain.”Celebs mourn Patrick Stewart's demiseTributes poured in on social media from all sections, including celebs, friends, former costars and even organisations that the late actor supported.Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy Body Dementia, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said. articles.title: Patrick Stewart, star of 'X-Men' and 'Star Trek,' dies at 86
articles.summary: The actor died Wednesday in Los Angeles after "a brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to a statement posted...
articles.body:
Patrick Stewart, a revered English actor best known for his work on Star Trek , has died. He was 86.

According to a post on his X account , Stewart died on Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles "in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia.

"He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," the post read. "We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.

"His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre. He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction's most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise," the post continued. "His professional accomplishments were humbly matched by his philanthropy and activism on behalf of human rights, survivors of domestic violence, global refugees, veterans' mental health services, and animal welfare, particularly his cherished foster puppies.

"He was a Knight, Chancellor, motor sport enthusiast, and lifelong Huddersfield Football fan," the post added. "He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion, and humanity he brought to every role — in his art and life."

Born on July 13, 1940, in Mirfield, Yorkshire, England, Stewart dropped out of school at age 15 to work as a reporter at a local newspaper and then furniture salesman before enrolling in drama school in 1957.

He made his professional theater debut in 1959, eventually joining the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966. He spent the next two decades performing in both classical and contemporary productions — Edward Albee's Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? ; Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra — alongside fellow stage greats such as Ben Kingsley and Helen Mirren.

In the mid '80s, Stewart moved to Los Angeles to star in Star Trek: The Next Generation , which ran from 1987 to 1994, as Captain Jean-Luc Picard.

He later reprised the role on the big screen for a series of Star Trek films, including Star Trek: Generations (1994), Star Trek: First Contact (1996), Star Trek: Insurrection (1998) and Star Trek: Nemesis (2002).

Stewart had more than 160 credits as an actor, according to IMDB , most recently as the voice of Avery Bullock on the animated comedy series American Dad!.

He will also appear posthumously in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday as Professor Charles Xavier, a role he played in several previous X-Men films.

In 2010, Stewart was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II and given the title of Sir in honor of his contributions to TV, film and theater.

"We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today," Hugh Jackman, who starred alongside Stewart in X-Men , wrote in an Instagram post . "And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days."

The Royal Shakespeare Company wrote on Instagram that Stewart was "a colossus of both stage and screen and one of the finest classical Shakespearean actors of his generation."

And William Shatner, who preceded Stewart as captain of Star Trek 's USS Enterprise, honored the talent and humanity that Stewart brought to the role of Picard.

"Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him," Shatner wrote on Instagram . "I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work."

Stewart had a son, Daniel, and daughter, Sophie, with his first wife, Sheila Falconer, who he married in 1966. They divorced in 1990.

In his 2023 memoir, Making It So , Stewart revealed that he had an affair with his Star Trek: The Next Generation costar Jennifer Hetrick during his marriage to Falconer, which led to their divorce and his estrangement from their children.

"We don't have relationships," Stewart told the Irish Independent during his book tour. "I never thought that this would happen, but both my children are in their 50s — they're not children anymore, they're adults. And my relationship with them is practically non-existent."

Stewart and Hetrick dated and were later engaged, but never married.

In 2000, he married Wendy Neuss, one of the show's producers. They divorced three years later, after Stewart had an affair with actress Lisa Dillon, his costar in a stage production of The Master Builder . At the time, Stewart was 62 and Dillon was 23.

"And so, another divorce. I felt stupid and responsible," Stewart wrote in his memoir. "I had cheated on my wife with a younger woman — again."

In 2008, Stewart met singer-songwriter Sunny Ozell at a restaurant in Brooklyn, where she was working as a waitress. Stewart was performing in a sold-out production of Macbeth , and gave her his phone number so he could arrange tickets for her.

"[I] said 'Call me, I can get a ticket.' And that's what we did. And she came backstage afterward and we had dinner and here we are," Stewart told People magazine .

They were married in 2013 in Ozell's home state of Nevada. Stewart's longtime friend and X-Men costar Ian McKellen officiated the ceremony.

articles.summary: El presentador de 'El Hormiguero' ha dedicado el inicio del programa de este jueves a las víctimas y sus familias, ha compartido su experiencia personal con el duelo y ha reclamado que se esclarezcan las causas de la tragedia
articles.body: Pablo Motos ha arrancado este jueves 'El Hormiguero' con un mensaje dedicado a las víctimas y a las familias afectadas por el grave accidente ferroviario ocurrido este miércoles en Urda, municipio de la provincia de Toledo, que se ha cobrado la vida hasta ahora de 69 personas. "Lo primero, por supuesto, las personas. Me imagino que igual que vosotros, no puedo dejar de pensar en las víctimas y en sus familias. Estábamos hablando antes que tenemos todos el cuerpo un poco cortado, de los vídeos y de todo lo que hemos visto. La vida sabe cómo hacernos sentir frágiles y solos cuando sabes que llega un cambio y que nada volverá a ser igual", ha comenzado diciendo Pablo Motos. "Hay una llamada de teléfono que muchos vamos a recibir alguna vez en la que nos van a decir que alguien a quien amamos con toda nuestra alma ya no va a volver a estar. Cuando te dicen que un ser querido tuyo ha muerto, sientes un dolor tan violento que tu mente lo anestesia y hasta te sientes culpable en los primeros momentos porque piensas que no estás sufriendo lo suficiente. Lo que pasa es que estás en shock y será en unas horas, y sobre todo en unos días, cuando sentirás un dolor insoportable porque te sientes solo y porque ahora en tu vida hay unos silencios que te destrozan", ha continuado el conductor de 'El Hormiguero'. "Esa persona no llamará a la hora que llamaba siempre, no oirás cómo suena su llave en la cerradura, no se sentará en su parte del sofá y tú no sabrás de dónde vas a sacar las fuerzas para seguir adelante. La verdad cruda es que una pérdida no se supera porque no vuelves a ser el mismo nunca. El duelo no es exactamente olvidar, es aprender a querer a alguien que ahora solamente está en tus recuerdos", ha indicado el de Requena. "Voy a decir algo íntimo por si os sirve. Cuando murieron mi padre y mi madre a mí me ayudaba mucho pensar en ellos siempre sonriendo. Parece un detalle pequeño pero en esos momentos es mucho. Con el tiempo empecé a preguntarme cómo me querrían ver ellos, si triste y sin ganas de luchar o feliz y saliendo adelante. Me ayudó y por eso lo quiero compartir porque igual también es útil para alguno de vosotros que esté pasando por uno de estos momentos. En segundo lugar hay que hablar de la gente, de cómo somos la gente cuando pasa algo así, que siempre sale lo mejor de nosotros. Ayer no había gente de izquierdas ni de derechas, solo había seres humanos ayudando a otros seres humanos, lo que subraya una vez más que el afecto lo cambia todo.", ha destacado Pablo Motos. "Y en tercer lugar están las respuestas. Para no añadir más dolor al que ya tienen las víctimas necesitan respuestas. Cuando uno se sube a un tren está confiando en el sistema, está confiando en que es seguro y nos han engañado, nos están intentando engañar. No puede haber un error humano si antes no hay un fallo técnico. Ha habido un error humano después de que los sistemas de seguridad antiguos hayan fallado y los sistemas de seguridad nuevos que debían de estar instalados no estaban instalados", ha subrayado el presentador. "La alta velocidad era el orgullo de España, el orgullo de España en el mundo entero, y hoy da miedo subirse a un tren. La pregunta es dónde está el dinero que se debería haber usado para el mantenimiento de estas infraestructuras. Hace cinco años la Unión Europea nos dio 160.000 millones de euros para modernizar todas las infraestructuras. ¿Dónde está el dinero? Basta de mentiras. Necesitamos y sobre todo las víctimas necesitan respuestas", ha proseguido. "Gracias, pero lo tenía que decir porque si no soy incapaz de hacer el programa esta noche Y dicho eso, aunque sea por un instante, vamos a tomarnos un descanso, vamos a intentar divertirnos un rato que seguro que nos aliviará y nos ayudará a pensar con un poco más de claridad", ha señalado Pablo Motos para concluir.

articles.title: Inside Denzel Washington and wife Pauletta’s real estate portfolio: From their 30,000-square-foot Beverly Park mansion to a $13 million New York apartment and historic Hollywood estate
